conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I understand you've been having epigastric pain and dry heaving for about a week?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, that’s right. It’s been really uncomfortable, especially the dry heaving. It’s worse than last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see you were admitted just last week for similar symptoms. Can you tell me if anything made it better or worse?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: The IV fluids helped last time. I’ve been trying to keep my G-tube feeds going, but I’ve been nervous about increasing the rate.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. We’ll start you on IV fluids again to rehydrate you and help settle your stomach.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thank you. Is this related to my gastric bypass or the G-tube?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It could be. Given your history, we’re concerned about gastritis or irritation at the gastrojejunal connection. But you’re not showing signs of obstruction.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I remember I had an ulcer there before. Could it be coming back?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s possible. We’re not doing an endoscopy this time, but we’ll treat it as if it’s inflammation or mild gastritis.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I be able to keep using my G-tube for feeds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll continue your G-tube feeds. In fact, we’ve scheduled an enteral infusion for later today at 55 ml/h with full-strength protein.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. I was worried I’d have to stop them again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll go slow and monitor you. We’ve also restarted your lansoprazole to reduce stomach acid and help the lining heal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m on rifaximin too—should I keep taking that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re continuing rifaximin. It helps with bacterial overgrowth, which can contribute to your symptoms.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my other meds—like fluoxetine and aripiprazole? I don’t want to miss doses.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All your regular medications are being given through the G-tube. We’ve confirmed they’re safe to crush or dissolve.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I’ve also been anxious about these episodes—feels like I’m losing control.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s completely understandable. We’re keeping your lorazepam available for anxiety, as prescribed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thanks. What about blood tests? Did they show anything wrong?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs came back normal. White count is fine, no infection. Kidney function and liver enzymes are stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No sign of dehydration this time?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You were a bit dehydrated when you arrived, but the IV fluids are correcting that. Your glucose and electrolytes are improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll need to be more careful with fluids between feeds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Small amounts of water or electrolyte solution between feeds can help.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better, actually. The nausea has calmed down since the IV fluids started.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Your vitals are stable, and you’ve had no fever. We’re going to keep the IV fluids running for a few more hours.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I try increasing the tube feed rate today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ve already started the enteral infusion at 55 ml/h. We’ll watch for any discomfort or reflux.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve done well with the tube feeds and no symptoms of pain or nausea. We’re planning to discharge you tomorrow if this continues.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. Will I need new medications?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re adding sucralfate four times a day. It coats the stomach and helps heal any irritation.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: How long should I take that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: For about four weeks. We’ll review it at your follow-up with Dr. Patel.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the pain medicine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll have oxycodone for breakthrough pain, but only if needed. Try the sucralfate and lansoprazole first.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve had a good night—no pain, vitals stable. We’re clearing you for discharge this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. Anything I should watch for at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If nausea or pain returns, slow the feeds and call your doctor. Keep taking sucralfate and your other meds as prescribed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And follow-up is with Dr. Patel?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, in one week. They’ll assess your progress and adjust treatment if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you for helping me feel better so quickly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and don’t hesitate to call if anything changes.
